identity.name: link_parcels
identity.description: Links permits to parcels via a 4-strategy cascade (address_points bridge exact 0.97, legacy parcels exact 0.95, name-only 0.80, spatial containment 0.90, spatial KNN-boundary fallback 0.65) and writes permit_parcels: a guarded composite-key upsert plus a per-batch keyed DELETE of superseded links (class F, link_full_retraction, LG-24), in one batch transaction.

why_lock.text: Lock 90 is not the spec number (this step's primary governing spec is 41, chain_permits). It was assigned by the c1ef0b73 advisory-lock retrofit and is recorded in src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts's registry ('scripts/link-parcels.js': 90) — kept textually per §5.4 so that registry stays green across the conversion.

why.text: Composite key (permit_num, revision_num, parcel_id), matching the live UNIQUE constraint (permit_parcels_permit_num_revision_num_parcel_id_key) — this is WHY a permit can legally carry 2+ rows (LP-D2's 989-row duplicate class is schema-legal, not constraint-violating). Guard names EXACTLY match_type + confidence, never linked_at (linked_at is the run clock, source:"run_at" — guarding on it would rewrite every row every run, the same D-5 class link_massing's own guard_columns comment names).

guard_why.text: LG-24 (Fold A B-1, 2026-08-30) — the DELETE-by-key half of Spec 122 §1.4's own class F ('upsert + DELETE stale + DELETE zero-match'). No IS DISTINCT FROM guard applies to a DELETE — the guard concept is for a value-overwrite, not a row removal. The scope IS the guard: a batch's own keyed DELETE only ever touches rows for permits in THAT batch, keyed by composite (permit_num, revision_num), excluding whichever parcel_id this batch's own upsert just kept.

write_discipline.scope: permit_num = ANY(batch keys) AND revision_num = ANY(batch keys) AND (keep_parcel_id IS NULL OR parcel_id != keep_parcel_id)

why.text: Genuinely unimplemented before this pilot (Fold A B-1): the schema enum names class F for both link_parcels (step 10) and link_massing (step 15), but link_massing never uses this mechanic — it uses set_based_scoped+guarded_upsert via an is_primary flag column permit_parcels does not have. writes[] declared ORDER (Fold B item 5): THIS entry fires AFTER the upsert above, inside the SAME executeUpsertBatch+executeGuardedDeleteByKey transaction — reversing the order would transiently leave the permit unlinked. The SQL text is compute-authored (buildMatchSql's delete_by_key_sql), mirroring set_based_join_update/insert_only_no_retraction/write_once_backfill's own descriptive-only split.

guard_why.text: LG-9/D-5 (2026-08-29 rule, parcel_buildings.linked_at incident): a run-clock column (columns[].source "run_at") may never sit in write_discipline.guard_columns — RUN_AT is DISTINCT FROM its own stored value on every run, so an IS DISTINCT FROM guard naming it is vacuous (never excludes anything) while LOOKING like a real guard, exactly the LG-9 trap. parcel_linked_at is this target's ONLY declared column, so there is no other column left to guard on — the honest declaration is guard:"none", matching LG-24's own sibling target (e2) shape. The scope IS the guard (same reasoning as e2's own guard_why): a batch's own watermark UPDATE only ever touches permit keys in THAT batch. The underlying compute-authored SQL (watermark_update_sql) additionally carries its own AND parcel_linked_at IS DISTINCT FROM $3 clause — a genuine, narrow safety net against a same-transaction retry re-stamping an already-current row — but that clause lives in the SQL text, not in this descriptor's own guard_columns, so LG-9's mechanical check (which only inspects columns[].source cross-referenced against guard_columns) correctly does not see it and does not need to.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9/D-5's mechanical check (parcel_buildings.linked_at incident, 2026-08-29) flags ANY run-clock column (columns[].source "run_at") sitting inside the EXPANDED guard_columns set, regardless of whether write_discipline.guard itself is "none" or "is_distinct_from" — this target's guard is already "none" (see guard_why above: parcel_linked_at is its ONLY declared column, so "all_declared" expands to exactly that one run-clock column, with nothing else to name instead). No guard mechanism reads guard_columns when guard:"none" — this field only exists here because the schema requires SOME value at this path, and "all_declared" is the honest one: it IS every declared column, there being only the one.

why.text: LP-D10 (WF6 output-panel finding, restored commit 10, 2026-08-30) — fence a21b7b01 (2026-04-01) RESTORED: 'Batch UPDATE parcel_linked_at = NOW() for ALL evaluated permits, regardless of match count' was dropped, nowhere-on-purpose, during commit 7's consolidation into LG-24's single transaction. This write is the WHOLE REASON the incremental filter (staleness.scope, below) can ever EXCLUDE a no-match permit — without it, an unmatchable permit is re-evaluated on every incremental run forever. Unconditional by design (every permit THIS BATCH processed, matched or not) — matching the old code's own literal unconditional overwrite exactly, not merely approximating it. writes[] declared ORDER (extends Fold B item 5): fires LAST, after the upsert (e1) and LG-24's keyed delete (e2), inside the SAME transaction — a permit's linked/unlinked state is already final before it is marked evaluated. The SQL text is compute-authored (buildMatchSql's watermark_update_sql), via the set_source:"compute" escape hatch (LG-22 precedent) — RUN_AT is a per-run bound value, not a declared constant, so the plain set_based_scoped codegen path (sqlLiteral) does not fit.

invalidates.when: any permit_parcels row for this permit gains a linked_at newer than permits.zoning_enriched_at — enrich_permits.js (Spec 66, permits-chain step 10, immediately downstream) re-derives the dominant linked parcel's zoning by-law feed onto permits via permit_parcels. Spec 66 DEC-3 declares an always-full relational join (no incremental filter, re-derived fresh on EVERY run) — so this edge is declarative documentation of the real dependency (Finding 2's correction: enrich_parcels does NOT consume permit_parcels; the real downstream consumer is enrich_permits), not a mechanism that literally gates enrich_permits's own scope.

why.text: Three write statements per batch, ONE transaction: the guarded upsert to permit_parcels (e1), LG-24's keyed DELETE from permit_parcels (e2), and LP-D10's restored permits.parcel_linked_at watermark UPDATE (e3, commit 10) — corrected from the '2, exactly two' claim that stood here through commit 9, which undercounted by omitting the watermark this same commit restores after it was found dropped at the WF6 output panel. The declared FULL-mode-only scoped mass retraction (W1, retract:"all"/retract_when:"full_only" on e1) is a FOURTH statement but fires at most once per run (before the batch loop), never per-batch.

staleness.scope: (street_num IS NOT NULL AND street_num != '' AND street_name IS NOT NULL AND street_name != '') OR (latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL) — further narrowed incrementally by (parcel_linked_at IS NULL OR (geocoded_at IS NOT NULL AND parcel_linked_at < geocoded_at))

why.text: A-1 RULED (Fold A, 2026-08-30) — the THIRD application of the link_massing A-8 / compute_centroids A-1(a) precedent in this programme (Spec 124 R-W). The pre-conversion JS (non-PostGIS) fallback (~46 lines: BBOX pre-filter, pointInGeoJSON ray-casting, haversineDistance) is a SECOND, independent implementation of the SAME centroid-nearest defect Finding 1 fixes — retired whole, not fixed, per Spec 124 R-W ('compute MUST NOT branch on PostGIS availability').

Both Strategy 3 Step 1 (ST_Contains) and Step 2 (THE FIX's KNN <-> operator) join on the live geometry directly — the exact column Strategy 3 Step 2's OLD predicate (parcels.centroid_lat/centroid_lng) never needed, and the exact reason this fix required a rung-(e) compute change rather than a rung (a)-(d) descriptor-only fix.

The KNN operator (pa.geom <-> point) and ST_Contains both seek this GiST index — without it Strategy 3 Step 2 degrades from the measured 400-500ms/batch to the struck co-resident-ST_DWithin form's 97.5s/batch or worse (Fold B item 1).
(permit_num, revision_num) → permits(permit_num, revision_num). The junction is only meaningful while both sides are referential.
parcel_id → parcels(id). Same class as the permit-side FK.

Measured live 2026-08-30: permit_parcels has relrowsecurity = true. Under any role that does not bypass RLS, the upsert and LG-24's DELETE both affect 0 rows WITH NO ERROR — same class as link_massing's own parcel_buildings finding, pilot 2's LR-D7.

why.text: LP-D12 (WF6 output-panel finding, observability seat, commit 12, 2026-08-30) — mirrors link_massing's own mass_retraction_ratio (compute/link-massing.js:520-529) verbatim: 'retracted and NOT rebuilt is the shape of a broken run.' Before this check, W1's own retraction count and rebuild count were both computed (written.e1.retracted / written.e1.inserted) but never reported anywhere a verdict could see — a FULL run that retracted spatial-tier links and then failed to relink them would read PASS on every other row. A genuine FULL run retracts N and rebuilds ~N (permits re-evaluate across all tiers, not only spatial), so this ratio is 0 in the normal case; a broken predicate, empty corpus, or half-completed run shows as non-zero.

why.text: LP-D9 (commit 8a, 2026-08-30). address_points_exact's JOIN originally matched on house-number + street-name ONLY (address_points carries no street-type column of its own) — a same-name-different-type collision (measured live: 26 MEADOWVALE RD vs DR, ~31.6km apart) could resolve to whichever candidate won the class/area/id-ASC tiebreak, regardless of the permit's own declared type. Measured system-wide before the fix: 7,062/215,552 (3.3%) currently-linked address_points_exact rows conflicted. THE FIX adds p.street_type_normalized to the JOIN, mirroring Strategy 1b's own empty-type predicate shape exactly. Post-fix a NEW mismatch is structurally impossible; this check is a standing whole-table audit (not merely run-scoped) so a pre-fix residual row an incremental run never revisits, or a future regression of the predicate, is never invisible again. WARN + retighten_when (Spec 48 §4.9), mirroring spatial_null_coordinate_permits' own convention.

why.text: T5 (LP-D4) — pre-conversion the floor was the bare literal 75 in parcelLinkRate>=75?'PASS':'WARN' with a duplicated '>= 75%' render string, zero registered logic_variables. Cumulative (a760e0e7's own reasoning), never run-scoped. Reported as the UNLINKED fraction (pct <= 25 on the complement is exactly link_rate >= 75), matching link_massing's own reporting convention. ⚠️ link_parcels_link_rate_warn_pct's own SEED VALUE is stored as the UNLINKED ceiling (default 25), NOT the link-rate floor (75) the old code's literal used — verdict.js's limit_from_config substitutes the config value directly into this check's pct<= form with no transform, and pct>= is documented there as unimplemented — so the config value itself must already be in complement terms for the substitution to be correct. Deviation from the plan's own 'default 75' text, for this hard architectural reason (verified live this commit: an un-transformed 75 substituted into pct<=75 would only WARN when unlinked exceeds 75%, i.e. linked below 25% — a materially looser, wrong bound, caught live when the real permits population measured 94.5% linked and incorrectly WARNed against the untransformed value).

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE is never correct — the junction is rebuilt, not reloaded. Re-run with LINK_PARCELS_FORCE_FULL=1, which forces mode full: the scoped mass retraction (match_type='spatial' only) clears the tier THE FIX changes and the same batch loop rebuilds it.

why.text: The normal outcome: mode resolved incremental, the batch loop ran, no FAIL/WARN row.
A WARN row stands (link_rate or spatial_null_coordinate_permits) and nothing FAILED. The run completed and wrote; the warning is in the table.
Mode resolved full (LINK_PARCELS_FORCE_FULL): W1's scoped mass retraction (match_type='spatial') ran before the batch loop. NOT reachable by any commit-7 invocation — commit 8's budgeted act.

WF6 output-panel finding (observability seat), corrected commit 11, 2026-08-30 — the terminal here used to be named "pre_write_refused", describing a when:"pre_write" check FAILing with no standing override. That mechanism is structurally unreachable for this step: all 14 declared checks[] are when:"post" (verified live, none pre_write), so makePreWriteGate returns null and the pre-write gate is a permanent no-op. Because this was the ONLY fail_check terminal, selectTerminal's own discriminator-miss fallback (narrowed=[] when no terminal id contains the failing check's own id, pool=byKind instead) silently selected it whenever ANY post-check FAILed — most plausibly write_privilege, stamping the false claim "no write was issued, permit_parcels is untouched" on a run whose writes DID execute (RLS-zeroed: every statement affects 0 rows with no error, the write happened, it just wrote nothing). Renamed and re-worded to match the correct, already-discriminator-matching shape link_massing.descriptor.json/link_wsib.descriptor.json both use for the SAME real failure mode: RLS is enabled on permit_parcels with zero policies and the role does not bypass it, so every statement affects 0 rows with no error. Without this the run is indistinguishable from one whose corpus had not changed.

LP-D12 (WF6 output-panel finding, observability seat, commit 12, 2026-08-30) — a FULL-mode run whose W1 mass retraction (writes[0], scope match_type='spatial') removed rows the same run's batch loop then failed to rebuild. The write already happened (both the retraction and whatever partial upsert the run managed), so this is a fail_check, not a pre_write refusal — mirrors link_massing's own failed_mass_retraction_ratio terminal (same class, same reasoning: 'the write already happened, which is why this terminal is failed rather than a pre_write refusal'). selectTerminal's discriminator (the failing check's own id, "parcel_retraction_ratio") correctly narrows to this terminal alone — id.includes("parcel_retraction_ratio") is true here and false for failed_write_privilege, so the two fail_check terminals never collide.
